$comment: Reviewer registry for this repository — a port of dotfiles/harness/review-attestation.json
through the ts-bridge adaptation, trimmed to the reviewers that measurably act here. The
SSOT of the SHAPE stays in dotfiles; kubelab, hive, web and ts-bridge each carry a copy.
Why the port was needed: this file did not exist, so `dotf pr triage-queue` could not answer
at all — `read reviewer registry: open harness/review-attestation.json: no such file or
directory` (measured 2026-09-06 before this file landed). Its exit status is 1 both when
triage is pending AND when the question cannot be computed, so an unanswerable queue is never
mistaken for a clear one; a file that answers is what turns the exit status into information.
review_markers ARE MEASURED HERE, NOT COPIED. Measured 2026-09-06 over every PR that exists
in this repository (#8-#23, fifteen PRs, no gaps except #20 which was never opened). CodeRabbit
posted on exactly three of them — it was enabled between #19 and #21 — so this measurement is
PROVISIONAL and should be re-read after ten more reviewed PRs. What it emits here, by PR:
## Walkthrough                              -> #21 #22 #23  (present on every CodeRabbit comment)
No actionable comments were generated...    -> #22          (clean review, dotfiles' marker)
## Review limit reached                     -> #23          (also carries 'rate limited by coderabbit.ai')
(no CodeRabbit output)                      -> #8-#19       (predates enablement; four are
release-please, one dependabot)
Two facts differ from the ts-bridge measurement and are recorded so nobody copies them back:
1. On #23 a SINGLE comment carries BOTH `## Review limit reached` and `## Walkthrough` — the
walkthrough is generated even when the review itself was rate limited. Here the walkthrough
therefore attests less than it does in ts-bridge, where the two were separate comments.
`## Walkthrough` is still the review marker because it is the only heading present on
every run; the decline markers are listed so the same comment also reads as declined.
2. `No actionable comments were generated` DOES appear here (#22), unlike ts-bridge (zero
matches there). It is not used as the marker because it appears only on the no-findings
path: #21 carried a real review with findings and does not contain it.
The `github-actions` entry declares an actor that is about to exist, not one that was
observed: .github/workflows/pr-agent.yml lands in the same PR as this file and NAN_API_KEY is
not yet set in this repository. Read the entry's own `why`; the first green run of pr-agent
on a PR here is the verification that makes it real.
Note the asymmetry that survives this: a CodeRabbit run that files ONLY a formal review with no
walkthrough comment still reads as 'no reviewer output yet'. That is a property of the tool, which
scans comments, and it is why pr-stewardship still asks a human to read the diff.

reviewers.why: ADVISORY, same disposition as the dotfiles, kubelab and ts-bridge registries: its REVIEW attests, its DECLINE does not refuse. CodeRabbit's quota is a third party's billing state rather than a property of the change; measured here 2026-09-06, one of the three PRs it has seen (#23) drew 'Review limit reached', so a decline that REFUSED would make the gate red for reasons the diff cannot fix and teach everyone to ignore it. An advisory decline yields `pending`, the honest answer: a reviewer that could not run is not a reviewer that refused. `## Review skipped` has not been observed here yet and is carried from the sibling ports because it is a documented CodeRabbit output, not a guess. LOGINS MATCH WITH TRAILING '[bot]' STRIPPED AND CASE FOLDED, because the two GitHub APIs disagree: REST reports coderabbitai[bot], GraphQL reports coderabbitai. The dotfiles 'no complaints' review marker is deliberately NOT reused -- see the $comment on review_markers.

PR-Agent (see .github/workflows/pr-agent.yml) runs under GITHUB_TOKEN and publishes through the COMMENTS api, so its reviews never enter reviews[] and a classifier that looked only at reviews would read every PR-Agent-reviewed PR as unattested. The marker is the `review` command's own heading. `## PR Code Suggestions` is deliberately NOT here — suggestions are not a review, which is also why auto_improve is off on the automatic path. MARKER PROVENANCE: verified in the sibling ports before being declared here — kubelab has 215 PR comments carrying '## PR Reviewer Guide' posted by github-actions[bot] (spot-checked on #1500, #1362) and dotfiles has 172. It has NEVER been observed in mail2markdown: the only github-actions[bot] comments here are release-please's 'Created releases' notices (#12, #15, #17, #19), which carry no heading and match nothing. The first green run of pr-agent on a mail2markdown PR is the verification, and until then this entry is a declaration of intent, not of an actor.

triage.why: The heading the pr-review-triage skill records its dispositions under, matched at line start. Declared once here and read back by `dotf pr triage-queue`, so the writer and the reader are not a two-file agreement nobody checks. Already in use here before this file existed: #22 and #23 each carry one. A disposition that lives only in a chat message evaporates, and the Definition of Done's Review item would then rest on a claim nobody can re-read. It is posted even when there was nothing to dispose of: 'CI green, no review findings' is a disposition, and leaving it unwritten is indistinguishable from nobody having looked.

escape.label: merged-unreviewed
escape.why: Both are required, never one. Proceeding on an unreviewed PR is allowed; proceeding SILENTLY is not. The label plus the section is what forces the disclosure into the durable record instead of a chat message.

signatures.name: release-please
signatures.why: Measured on #12, #15, #17 and #19: exactly these four paths on every one, because release-please-config.json bumps the version in pyproject.toml and the package __init__ in addition to the manifest and changelog. Matched by DIFF SIGNATURE with set equality, never by author or branch — the author here is github-actions[bot] under the workflow token and the branch is release-please--branches--master, but an author rule would break the day the workflow moves to a PAT and a branch rule would let any branch named to match walk past the gate. The moment such a PR touches one more file the exemption stops applying, and it stops applying just as surely if one declared file is not touched. This is not 'small PRs need no review': a release commit mechanically restates commits that were each reviewed when they landed, and reporting `declined` on it says something false.
